confusions: The skill says 'write a new policy with the template's rules'; the 'Keep code easy to review' recipe says 'one policy per template' but also gives one policy with its own key for extra rules. Unclear which applies when only some templates of a recipe fit the ask.
The template CONV-040 limits (30 statements) were a hint; there is no guidance on picking a limit from a '200 line' complaint. I guessed the template's default.

LOG-010's template is titled and scoped to api.request, but the limits note says to add other outbound statements. The skill says to cover all of them; it is unclear whether a partial rule counts as coverage. I used the template rule as written and flagged the gap.
CHG-001 template says 'every endpoint' but its first rule is object_kinds query only. Extending it to function was my call; the skill does not say whether functions should be added to a template.

The skill says 'Write only names the catalogue and workspace have' and 'tag only if the workspace has it'; no guidance on whether a policy with no tags needs tags for the 'owner' or 'classification' parts of the customer's ask.

xano policy parse text output omitted the severity line for LOG-010 while it printed it for CHG-001 and CONV-040; the -o json output has severity 'medium'. Looks like a display quirk; recorded as a confusion, not a parse error.
No check for missing null checks or error handling in functions; the customer's most common review item is not covered and the skill does not offer a fallback.
wished_for: A recipe for 'code review hygiene' that picks the three or four templates most dev leads ask for, with the statement wording and size limits explained.
Guidance on mapping 'lines' in a customer's ask to statements, with a worked example of a 200-line function.
A check or template for generic error handling in functions (not just external calls), or an explicit 'not checkable' entry for it.
A note on whether a template's rules may be extended to more object kinds, and how to say so in the statement.
An example of an advisory-first rollout (what to say the owner must decide before making it blocking).
why_confidence: The three rules are valid and parse cleanly, and they cover tests, function size and external-call error handling, which are the checkable parts of the ask. Confidence is only medium because general error handling, runtime behaviour and the review process are not checkable, and I did not run policy evaluate, so the matches are predictions.
